Keywords: Night watches and company for river traders
RagShortTexts: River trading vessels could face interception at narrow channels and landings.
Extra guards, waiting for company and detours each increased costs or delay.

Variants.Content: Trading vessels could face armed interception. Narrow channels, landings and tired crews shaped their response. Owners arranging company, watches and handovers weighed escort costs against delays to a voyage.

Trading vessels could face armed interception. Narrow channels, landings and tired crews shaped their response. Owners arranging company, watches and handovers weighed escort costs against delays to a voyage. Crews and guards organized watches and shore parties. Pursuit left goods and wounded people behind; risks depended on personnel, vessel and the next safe landing.

Trading vessels could face armed interception. Narrow channels, landings and tired crews shaped their response. Owners arranging company, watches and handovers weighed escort costs against delays to a voyage. Authorities tolerating raids gained immediate property but lost traffic and invited reprisals. River income needed guards, negotiation and restraint of their own fighters.

Owners arranging company, watches and handovers weighed escort costs against delays to a voyage. Boatmen, handlers and food providers depended on traffic. Interrupted travel reduced livelihoods, while hosting victims and refugees strained stores and lodging.
